newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Red Cross hands over bodies of Sri Lanka servicemen.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross hands over bodies of Sri Lanka servicemen.

text.p: The bodies of eight Sri Lankan servicemen, who went missing after Tamil rebels attacked their boat, were handed to the military by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), a spokesman said on Saturday.
"We approached the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) about the fate of the eight missing people and the LTTE's reply came saying they were all dead," an ICRC spokesman told Reuters.
He said the rebels handed over the bodies of five navy personnel and three policemen to the ICRC on Friday morning.
The ICRC handed over the bodies to military authorities at Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) northeast of Colombo, the same afternoon, he added.

The eight servicemen went missing after boats from the LTTE's Sea Tiger naval wing attacked two navy boats on Thursday in the waters off northwestern Mannar Island, about 240 km (150 miles) north of Colombo, military officials said.
One sailor was killed and the boat carrying the eight servicemen was believed to have been captured by the rebels, they said.

The LTTE, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, did not suffer any casualties, the rebels' official radio broadcast said on Friday.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
